docs.title: Hydrogen — standalone reference panels
docs.text: title: Hydrogen — standalone reference panels record id: MAT:0001 status: RESEARCHED IN PROGRESS Hydrogen — standalone reference panels The light educational set contains nine separate panels; the dark blueprint set contains thirteen. Both are required. A panel becomes available here after individual visual review. These illustrations supplement the locked V01–V18 manifest. A01 — Atomic Structure Neutral protium: one proton, zero neutrons, one electron. Simplified Bohr schematic, not a literal electron path; not to scale. Species: isolated neutral protium (¹H). Nuclear identity follows NUBASE2020 (SRC 000008); neutral electron count follows Z − q, consistent with the NIST evaluation (SRC 000005). The circular line is a teaching convention, not a measured trajectory. Charges shown are in elementary charge units. A02 — Electron Probability Cloud (1s) Qualitative Hydrogen ground state 1s probability density cloud, darkest at the centre and fading outward; not to scale. This illustrates the ideal nonrelativistic Coulomb 1s model already described in the Hydrogen chapter. The density is proportional to exp(−2r/a), with a the model's Bohr length scale, and has its maximum at the nucleus. The radial shell probability also includes the 4πr² factor and has a different maximum. Neither the painted brightness nor its pixel radius supplies a measured value. NIST (SRC 000005) supports the ground state identity; it is not the source of this painted density field. A03 — H₂ Molecule Hydrogen molecule bonding schematic: two H atoms with one shared electron pair; single covalent bond, not to scale. Species: neutral molecular Hydrogen, H₂. The NIST Chemistry WebBook molecular entry (SRC 000010) provides the molecular identity and ground state context. The two electron symbols are a shared pair teaching convention; they do not indicate measured positions or trajectories. The lobes are not calibrated molecular orbital density surfaces. No bond length or dissociation energy is inferred from the image. A04 — Isotopes Protium, deuterium and tritium nuclei with one proton each and zero, one and two neutrons respectively; neutral atoms each have one electron. Nucleon counts and stable/radioactive classifications follow the ground state entries for ¹H, ²H and ³H in NUBASE2020 (SRC 000008). A neutral Hydrogen atom has one electron because Z = 1 and q = 0 (SRC 000005). The nuclei are schematic and not to scale. Abundances vary with material and are deliberately not supplied by this diagram. The three isotope sub diagrams are components of this single A04 asset. B09 — 3D Extruded Data Object Hydrogen conceptual data sculpture with identity, properties and connections rings. Not a physical model of an atom. This standalone dark blueprint panel follows the supplied template's data object design. H and Z = 1 identify Hydrogen (SRC 000005). The glass, metal, rings and pedestal are visual metaphors for organising information. They are not measured material properties, a physical atomic model, an energy apparatus or evidence for a speculative mechanism. The artwork does not assert that the data record is complete. Remaining panels A05–A09, B01–B08 and B10–B13 remain pending. Their exact separate image requirements and crosswalk to V01–V18 are tracked in the panel image plan. Neither the supplied composite posters nor existing supplementary artwork count as these separate deliverables.

docs.title: Hydrogen — People and Intellectual Lineage
docs.text: Hydrogen — People and Intellectual Lineage Purpose Hydrogen science did not arise from one discovery. MAT distinguishes: This prevents attribution from becoming a simple list of famous names. 1. Early Hydrogen Chemistry Robert Boyle Role: Contribution: Described production of the gas later recognized as hydrogen through reactions involving metals and acids in the seventeenth century. MAT does not assign Boyle sole discovery of hydrogen as an element. Henry Cavendish Role: Contribution: Systematically studied what he called inflammable air and established important physical and chemical characteristics of the gas. Common historical attribution gives Cavendish major credit for identifying hydrogen as a distinct substance. Antoine Lavoisier Role: Contribution: Placed hydrogen into the developing modern chemical framework and gave it the name derived from its relationship to water formation. 2. Hydrogen Spectroscopy Johann Jakob Balmer Role: Contribution: Identified the mathematical regularity of the visible atomic hydrogen spectral series now called the Balmer series. Relationship: Johannes Rydberg Role: Contribution: Generalized the mathematical description of atomic spectral series. Hydrogen became a central test system for the Rydberg relationship. Niels Bohr Role: Contribution: Used hydrogen as the central atomic example in the early quantized atomic model. The Bohr model is historically important and predicts major hydrogen energy level relationships. MAT classifies it as: rather than the final modern quantum description. 3. Modern Quantum Description The following contributors are primarily linked through the scientific principles used to describe hydrogen rather than through discovery of Hydrogen itself. Max Planck Relationship: Erwin Schrödinger Relationship: Hydrogen became one of the principal exactly solvable quantum systems of the Schrödinger framework. Max Born Relationship: Relevant to: Werner Heisenberg Relationship: Wolfgang Pauli Relationship: Paul Dirac Relationship: 4. Electromagnetism and Field Response Michael Faraday Relevant to: electromagnetic induction; field concepts; electrochemistry. James Clerk Maxwell Relevant to: Hydrogen spectroscopy, radiation and plasma behavior rely on electromagnetic theory. Hendrik Lorentz Relevant to: \mathbf F = q( \mathbf E+\mathbf v\times\mathbf B ) and charged hydrogen/plasma states. Pieter Zeeman Relationship: Johannes Stark Relationship: 5. Hydrogen Isotopes Harold C. Urey Role: Urey led the scientific search that established heavy hydrogen. He received the 1934 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for the discovery. George M. Murphy Role: Murphy worked with Urey on the spectroscopic identification of heavy hydrogen. Ferdinand G. Brickwedde Role: Brickwedde produced enriched liquid hydrogen fractions at the National Bureau of Standards that enabled the heavy isotope's spectral signature to become clearly measurable. Edward W. Washburn Role: Associated with subsequent electrolytic enrichment/separation work involving deuterium. 6. Tritium and Heavy Hydrogen Nuclear Physics Ernest Rutherford Role: Mark Oliphant Role: Paul Harteck Role: Rutherford, Oliphant and Harteck published major 1934 experiments on transmutation using heavy hydrogen. These experiments form part of the historical lineage of hydrogen isotope nuclear physics and tritium production. 7. Cryogenic Hydrogen James Dewar Role: Contribution: Successfully liquefied hydrogen in 1898 and subsequently produced solid hydrogen. This forms part of the intellectual lineage of: 8. Precision Hyperfine Measurement The following researchers are linked directly to the precision Hydrogen hyperfine measurement used by MAT: Relationship: Reported frequency: 1\,420\,405\,751.768\ {\rm Hz} 9. Modern H₂ Thermodynamics J. W. Leachman R. T. Jacobsen S. G. Penoncello E. W. Lemmon Role: Contribution: Reference equations of state for: These models are used in the MAT thermodynamic branch rather than treating all molecular hydrogen as one state. 10. Modern ⁶H Measurement The 2025 MAMI A1 experiment includes: Role: Relationship: The result is kept separate from NUBASE2020 until a later evaluated nuclear data release reconciles it. 11. Wider Scientific Principle Lineage The legacy Hydrogen record lists additional people connected to principles used by MAT: These names should not automatically receive: relationships. Instead they link to the relevant: used by the Hydrogen record. 12. Historical / Unverified Overlay Contributors Legacy G0001 also lists: MAT retains these only in the: layer. Their proposed relationships must not be represented as established hydrogen physics without independent reproducible evidence. 13. Replicators and Extenders MAT uses the word: for a researcher or team that independently reproduces an earlier result. It uses: for work that takes an established result and expands its precision, theory, domain or application. These are distinct from: or: 14. Attribution Rule A Hydrogen record may therefore have a chain such as: All roles may belong to different people.

This is scoped reference coverage; the element remains under scientific review. Parent Helium record Structured values and provenance Retained source export · SRC 000005 NIST definitions and qualifiers State and evidence semantics Each threshold removes one electron from an isolated ground state atom or ion of charge q, producing charge q+1. Electron count is calculated as Z−q. This is not a bulk work function or electrochemical potential. Square brackets retain semiempirical estimates; parentheses retain theoretical values. Unbracketed values retain their evaluated status. Ground configurations describe dominant calculated components and may have uncertain assignments. NIST notation is preserved. Numeric uncertainty is transcribed in eV; unavailable uncertainty remains UNKNOWN. No confidence level, isotope assignment or extra precision is inferred. Derived decay metrics The structured evaluation now includes a decay constant and mean lifetime for each positive numeric half life. Result: VALIDATION 018 — Visual Slots Result: Final Helium Status After the He₂ correction and all files in this batch are added: Helium can then serve as MAT's second validated reference element. It specifically validates schema features that Hydrogen could not: I checked the actual pre migration G0002 from its Git history rather than reconstructing it from memory. Its middle sections cover Pauli structure, excited states, spectroscopy, the ³He magnetic channel, He I/He II, pressure dependent solidification, ³He superfluidity and extreme pressure chemistry; the latter sections cover the environment matrix, technology/energy roles, geometry, Hydrogen–Helium relationship dimensions and evidence classification. The one substantive correction is the He₂ point above: a bound neutral \(^{4}\mathrm{He} 2\) state is experimentally established, but it is extraordinarily weak and does not overturn the statement that ordinary bulk Helium is monatomic. ([Nature][5])

docs.title: Helium — People and Intellectual Lineage
docs.text: Helium — People and Intellectual Lineage Pierre Janssen Role: Associated with observation of the solar spectral line that preceded terrestrial isolation of Helium. Norman Lockyer Role: Interpreted the solar spectral feature as evidence for a previously unknown element. Edward Frankland Role: Associated with the naming of Helium with Lockyer. William Ramsay Role: Linked to establishing Helium on Earth through gas released from mineral material. Per Teodor Cleve and Abraham Langlet Role: Part of the independent terrestrial Helium identification lineage. Heike Kamerlingh Onnes Role: In 1908 Onnes successfully produced liquid Helium, opening a major new low temperature regime. ([Nobel Prize][3]) Pyotr Kapitza Role: Kapitza's experiments established the extraordinary flow behavior of He II and identified it as a superfluid. ([Nobel Prize][4]) John F. Allen Role: A. D. Misener Role: Allen and Misener independently reported the unusual flow behavior of liquid Helium II in the same historical period as Kapitza. Lev Landau Role: Developed the theoretical description of quantum collective excitations in liquid Helium, including the phonon/roton framework. ([Nobel Prize][5]) David M. Lee Douglas D. Osheroff Robert C. Richardson Role: Their 1972 experiments established superfluid phases of ³He. They shared the 1996 Nobel Prize in Physics for that discovery. ([Nobel Prize][6]) Anthony J. Leggett Role: Linked to theoretical understanding of superfluid ³He and more general macroscopic quantum phenomena. Classification Rule Do not collapse these roles into: The lineage distinguishes: These are different contributions.

docs.title: Lithium — People and Intellectual Lineage
docs.text: Lithium — People and Intellectual Lineage Johan August Arfwedson Role: Contribution: Identified Lithium as a new alkali element while analysing petalite in 1817. Jöns Jacob Berzelius Role: Arfwedson worked in Berzelius's laboratory. William Thomas Brande Role: Produced a small quantity of Lithium metal electrolytically in 1821. Robert Bunsen Role: Augustus Matthiessen Role: Bunsen and Matthiessen obtained sufficient bulk Lithium by electrolysis of molten Lithium chloride in 1855. John Cockcroft Role: Ernest Walton Role: Their accelerated proton experiment on Lithium demonstrated artificial nuclear transmutation and produced alpha particles. Lithium Ion Battery Lineage M. Stanley Whittingham Role: Contribution: Developed an early rechargeable Lithium battery using a host structure capable of reversible Lithium insertion. John B. Goodenough Role: Contribution: Developed high voltage Lithium cobalt oxide cathode chemistry, greatly increasing useful cell voltage. Akira Yoshino Role: Contribution: Developed a practical rechargeable architecture using carbonaceous negative electrode materials rather than metallic Lithium. Relationship chain: Foundational Principle Lineage Lithium also inherits principles associated with: These contributors link to equations, theories or methods used in Lithium science. They are not automatically classified as Lithium discoverers. Historical / Unverified Overlay If legacy Russell material is retained, classify: It must not modify the measured Lithium core. docs.title: Beryllium — People and Intellectual Lineage
docs.text: Beryllium — People and Intellectual Lineage René Just Haüy Role: Haüy suspected that beryl and emerald contained an unknown constituent and encouraged chemical investigation. Louis Nicolas Vauquelin Role: In 1798 Vauquelin identified the new element in beryl/emerald material. He did not isolate pure metallic Beryllium. Friedrich Wöhler Role: Wöhler isolated metallic Beryllium in 1828 through reduction chemistry involving Beryllium chloride. Antoine Bussy Role: Bussy independently isolated metallic Beryllium in 1828. MAT therefore distinguishes: from: Neutron Discovery Lineage Walther Bothe Role: Herbert Becker Role: Bothe and Becker observed unusually penetrating radiation when Beryllium was bombarded with alpha particles. Irène Joliot Curie Role: Frédéric Joliot Curie Role: The Joliot Curies showed that Beryllium radiation could eject energetic protons from hydrogen containing material. James Chadwick Role: Chadwick demonstrated in 1932 that the penetrating radiation was consistent with a neutral massive particle: Relationship: Beryllium therefore has a direct place in the experimental lineage of neutron discovery. Additional Principle Lineage Beryllium science also draws on principles associated with: These people are linked to theories, measurement methods or scientific frameworks. They are not all direct Beryllium discoverers. docs.title: Boron — Ground States and Ionisation Ladder
docs.text: Boron — Ground States and Ionisation Ladder Dated NIST ASD 5.12 extraction, retrieved 14 September 2026. 5 charge state rows and 5 numeric ionisation energies are present. This is scoped reference coverage; the element remains under scientific review. Parent Boron record Structured values and provenance Retained source export · SRC 000005 NIST definitions and qualifiers State and evidence semantics Each threshold removes one electron from an isolated ground state atom or ion of charge q, producing charge q+1. Electron count is calculated as Z−q. This is not a bulk work function or electrochemical potential. Square brackets retain semiempirical estimates; parentheses retain theoretical values. Unbracketed values retain their evaluated status. Ground configurations describe dominant calculated components and may have uncertain assignments. NIST notation is preserved. Numeric uncertainty is transcribed in eV; unavailable uncertainty remains UNKNOWN. No confidence level, isotope assignment or extra precision is inferred. Isotope shifts, excited state thresholds, material properties and later literature remain separate work. Ionisation ladder chart Discrete ground state ionisation thresholds by initial charge, coloured by evidence status; logarithmic energy axis. Generated from the structured evaluation above. Missing energies occupy a separate axis strip, not zero energy. Reported uncertainties are shown where valid on the logarithmic axis; missing uncertainties remain unknown. The source table retains exact notation and source line locators. Calculated energy equivalents The structured entries include f = E/h and the energy equivalent vacuum wavelength λ = hc/E, converting eV to joules with the exact elementary charge. The SI defining constants are registered as SRC 000302. Frequency uncertainty propagates linearly; wavelength uncertainty uses the first order reciprocal derivative. Missing source uncertainty remains UNKNOWN. These are mathematical energy equivalents, not observed spectral lines, universal element frequencies or recoil corrected photoionisation thresholds. Theoretical and semiempirical input status is retained; floating point digits do not imply additional precision.

CALC-001 — Boron-10 Neutron Capture Ground-State Q-Value
docs.text: CALC 001 — Boron 10 Neutron Capture Ground State Q Value Reaction: {}^{10}B+n \rightarrow {}^7Li+{}^4He Atomic masses: m({}^{10}B) = 10.01293695\ {\rm u} m n = 1.00866491595\ {\rm u} m({}^7Li) = 7.0160034366\ {\rm u} m({}^4He) = 4.00260325413\ {\rm u} The atomic electron count balances between reactants and products. Mass difference: \Delta m = m({}^{10}B)+m n m({}^7Li) m({}^4He) \Delta m \approx 0.00299541462\ {\rm u} Using: 1u\,c^2 = 931.49410372\ {\rm MeV} gives: \boxed{ Q \approx 2.7899881\ {\rm MeV} } This is the total ground state reaction Q value.

docs.title: CALC-002 — Dominant Boron-10 Capture Branch
docs.text: CALC 002 — Dominant Boron 10 Capture Branch A dominant thermal neutron capture branch produces excited Lithium 7: {}^{10}B+n \rightarrow {}^7Li^ +\alpha followed by: {}^7Li^ \rightarrow {}^7Li+\gamma with the gamma energy approximately: E \gamma \approx 0.478\ {\rm MeV} The available kinetic energy before gamma emission is therefore approximately: Q {\rm kinetic} \approx 2.790 0.478 \boxed{ Q {\rm kinetic} \approx 2.312\ {\rm MeV} } while the complete final state energy release remains the full reaction Q value: \approx2.790\ {\rm MeV} Reference branching fraction near the thermal neutron standard region: f {\rm excited} \approx 0.937 The branch fraction is neutron energy dependent and must retain its reference conditions.

docs.title: CALC-003 — Proton–Boron-11 Reaction Q-Value
docs.text: CALC 003 — Proton–Boron 11 Reaction Q Value Reaction: {}^1H+{}^{11}B \rightarrow 3\,{}^4He Using atomic masses: m({}^1H) = 1.00782503223\ {\rm u} m({}^{11}B) = 11.00930536\ {\rm u} m({}^4He) = 4.00260325413\ {\rm u} Electron accounting balances when neutral atomic masses are used. Mass difference: \Delta m = m({}^1H)+m({}^{11}B) 3m({}^4He) giving: \boxed{ Q \approx 8.682112\ {\rm MeV} } The principal reaction products are three alpha particles. Scientific interpretation: Engineering interpretation: DOE notes that proton–Boron fusion requires substantially higher ion temperatures than D–T fusion.

docs.title: Boron — People and Intellectual Lineage
docs.text: Boron — People and Intellectual Lineage Louis Joseph Gay Lussac Role: In 1808 Gay Lussac and Thénard produced an impure elemental Boron preparation through reduction chemistry. Louis Jacques Thénard Role: Worked independently of Davy's London work in the 1808 Boron isolation period. Humphry Davy Role: Davy independently obtained Boron containing elemental material in 1808. The historical products were not today's standard of ultra high purity elemental Boron. Henri Moissan Role: Produced purer Boron later in the nineteenth century. Ezekiel Weintraub Role: Produced highly purified Boron using Boron halide/hydrogen processing. Borane and Multicentre Bonding Lineage William N. Lipscomb Role: Lipscomb and collaborators determined Borane structures and developed a deeper understanding of their unusual electron deficient bonding. His work showed that conventional two centre/two electron bonding alone could not adequately explain the Borane family. He received the 1976 Nobel Prize in Chemistry: MAT relationship: Kenneth Wade Role: Wade developed electron counting rules linking skeletal electron pair counts to families of polyhedral cluster structures. Canonical classes include: For a closo cluster with \(n\) vertices: N {\rm SEP}=n+1 skeletal electron pairs. The rules are structural predictors and organizing principles. They are not universal laws for every Boron containing structure. D. Michael P. Mingos Role: Extended and generalized cluster electron counting concepts across main group and transition metal cluster chemistry. Eluvathingal D. Jemmis Role: Developed the mno framework for condensed/macropolyhedral cluster systems. This extends the intellectual lineage from isolated polyhedra toward connected cluster architectures. High Pressure Boron Lineage Artem R. Oganov Role: Associated with the identification and structural interpretation of \(\gamma B {28}\). Jiuhua Chen Role: Associated with experimental characterization of \(\gamma B {28}\). Carlo Gatti Role: Contributed to analysis of the unusual bonding/charge transfer character in \(\gamma B {28}\). Extreme Pressure Superconductivity Mikhail I. Eremets Role: Viktor V. Struzhkin Role: Ho kwang Mao Role: Russell J. Hemley Role: Their experimental work established pressure induced metallic/superconducting Boron at megabar class pressures. Foundational Principle Lineage Boron additionally inherits principle links to: These are principle/theory contributors. They are not automatically Boron discoverers. Replicator Rule MAT permits: where evidence supports those roles. Do not assign REPLICATOR merely because a later scientist worked on the same subject. Historical / Unverified Layer If Walter Russell material from the legacy record is retained: It must remain outside the validated scientific core.

docs.title: CALC-001 — Triple-Alpha Net Q-Value
docs.text: CALC 001 — Triple Alpha Net Q Value Net reaction: \[ 3\,{}^4He \rightarrow {}^{12}C \] Using: \[ m({}^4He)=4.00260325413\ u \] and: \[ m({}^{12}C)=12\ u \] the mass difference is: \[ \Delta m = 3m({}^4He) m({}^{12}C) \] \[ = 0.00780976239\ u \] Using: \[ 1u\,c^2=931.49410372\ {\rm MeV} \] gives: \[ \boxed{ Q = 7.274748\ {\rm MeV} } \] The stellar reaction proceeds through intermediate nuclear states, especially transient 8Be and the resonant 12C Hoyle state. The net Q value must not be confused with the Hoyle state excitation energy.

docs.title: CALC-002 — Carbon-14 Beta Decay Q-Value
docs.text: CALC 002 — Carbon 14 Beta Decay Q Value Reaction: {}^{14}C \rightarrow {}^{14}N + e^ + \bar{\nu} e Using neutral atomic masses: m({}^{14}C) = 14.0032419884\ u m({}^{14}N) = 14.00307400443\ u gives: \Delta m = 0.00016798397\ u and: \boxed{ Q \beta \approx 0.1564761\ {\rm MeV} } or approximately: 156.476\ {\rm keV} This is the total beta decay energy available to the decay products. It is not the energy of every emitted electron. The beta particles occupy a continuous energy spectrum because energy and momentum are shared with the antineutrino and recoiling daughter.

docs.title: CALC-003 — Carbon-14 Decay Constant
docs.text: CALC 003 — Carbon 14 Decay Constant Using the adopted MAT reference: t {1/2} = 5700\ {\rm y} the decay constant is: \lambda = \frac{\ln2}{t {1/2}} giving approximately: \boxed{ \lambda \approx 1.216\times10^{ 4}\ {\rm y^{ 1}} } The activity relationship is: A=\lambda N and radioactive population evolves as: N(t)=N 0e^{ \lambda t} The conventional Libby radiocarbon age scale must use its own method defined half life rather than silently replacing the physical half life in this calculation.

docs.title: Carbon — People and Intellectual Lineage
docs.text: Carbon — People and Intellectual Lineage Antoine Lavoisier Role: Lavoisier's combustion studies helped establish Carbon as an elemental substance and connected diamond combustion with carbon dioxide formation. Smithson Tennant Role: Tennant demonstrated that diamond and ordinary carbonaceous material produce the same Carbon dioxide product under combustion, strengthening the conclusion that diamond is Carbon. Carbon 14 / Chronology Willard F. Libby Role: Developed the method of using Carbon 14 decay for age determination. Nobel Prize in Chemistry: MAT contribution: Source: Stellar Carbon / Hoyle State Fred Hoyle Role: Predicted the need for a resonant excited state of ¹²C to explain efficient stellar Carbon production. Canonical state: Source: Fullerenes Harold Kroto Role: Robert Curl Role: Richard Smalley Role: Their 1985 work established the C₆₀ fullerene family. They shared the 1996 Nobel Prize in Chemistry. Source: James R. Heath Role: Sean C. O'Brien Role: MAT preserves discovery team participation separately from Nobel attribution. Carbon Nanotubes Sumio Iijima Role: His 1991 electron microscopy work reported coaxial graphitic nanotubes and established the modern CNT research field. Source: Earlier tubular Carbon observations remain part of the historical precursor lineage and should not be erased. Graphene Andre Geim Role: Konstantin Novoselov Role: Their 2004 experiments isolated and characterized graphene. They shared the 2010 Nobel Prize in Physics. Source: Raman / Carbon Nanoscience Mildred S. Dresselhaus Role: Her work helped establish Raman spectroscopy as a quantitative tool for Carbon nanotubes, graphite and graphene related materials. Source: Gene Dresselhaus Role: Ado Jorio Role: Andrea C. Ferrari Role: The 2006 graphene Raman work demonstrates how spectral structure can recover information about layer number and electronic state. Sources: Principle Lineage Carbon also inherits principle level relationships to: These are theory/principle relationships. They are not Carbon discovery roles. CALC-001 — Nitrogen-13 Positron-Decay Q-Value
docs.text: CALC 001 — Nitrogen 13 Positron Decay Q Value Reaction: {}^{13}N \rightarrow {}^{13}C+e^++\nu e Using neutral atomic masses: m({}^{13}N)=13.00573861\ u m({}^{13}C)=13.00335483507\ u For positron decay using atomic masses: Q {\beta^+} = [ M({}^{13}N) M({}^{13}C) 2m e ]c^2 giving approximately: \boxed{ Q {\beta^+} \approx 1.19847\ {\rm MeV} }

docs.title: CALC-002 — Nitrogen-16 Beta-Minus Total Q-Value
docs.text: CALC 002 — Nitrogen 16 Beta Minus Total Q Value Reaction: {}^{16}N \rightarrow {}^{16}O+e^ +\bar\nu e Using neutral atomic masses: m({}^{16}N)=16.0061019\ u m({}^{16}O)=15.99491461957\ u gives: \boxed{ Q {\beta^ } \approx 10.4209\ {\rm MeV} } This is the total decay energy window. It is not the energy of every beta particle or every gamma photon. The important 6.12863 MeV gamma belongs to a particular daughter state de excitation branch.

docs.title: CALC-003 — Nitrogen-17 Beta-Minus Q-Value
docs.text: CALC 003 — Nitrogen 17 Beta Minus Q Value {}^{17}N \rightarrow {}^{17}O+e^ +\bar\nu e Using atomic masses: \boxed{ Q {\beta^ } \approx 8.6790\ {\rm MeV} } The daughter can be populated above its neutron separation threshold. This enables: {}^{17}O^ \rightarrow {}^{16}O+n which explains the large beta delayed neutron branch. NUBASE2020: P {\beta n} = 95.1\pm0.7\%

docs.title: Nitrogen — People and Intellectual Lineage
docs.text: Nitrogen — People and Intellectual Lineage Henry Cavendish Role: Produced Nitrogen rich residual gas through removal of reactive components from air. He did not establish it as a new element. Joseph Priestley Role: Also obtained gas depleted in oxygen and observed its inability to sustain ordinary combustion or animal respiration. Daniel Rutherford Role: In 1772 Rutherford described the residual gas and recognized it as a distinct component of air. MAT distinguishes: from: Source: Antoine Lavoisier Role: Associated with the historical name: reflecting the inability of Nitrogen rich air to sustain animal life. Jean Antoine Chaptal Role: Coined the name: Source: Industrial Nitrogen Fixation Fritz Haber Role: Established practical laboratory synthesis: N 2+3H 2 \rightleftharpoons 2NH 3 under elevated pressure and temperature. Nobel Prize in Chemistry: Source: Robert Le Rossignol Role: Worked with Haber on the laboratory apparatus used to demonstrate continuous ammonia synthesis. Carl Bosch Role: Converted Haber’s laboratory chemistry into industrial high pressure ammonia production. Nobel Prize in Chemistry: Source: Alwin Mittasch Role: Led extensive catalyst development work associated with industrial ammonia synthesis. Source: Gerhard Ertl Role: Used modern surface science methods to establish detailed mechanisms of catalytic reactions on solid surfaces, including key steps in ammonia synthesis on iron. Nobel Prize in Chemistry: Source: Biological Nitrogen Fixation Hermann Hellriegel Role: Hermann Wilfarth Role: Their experiments established the special relationship between legumes, root nodules and acquisition of atmospheric Nitrogen. Source: Martinus Willem Beijerinck Role: Isolated and characterized root nodule bacteria involved in symbiotic Nitrogen fixation. Source: Polymeric Nitrogen Mikhail I. Eremets Role: Alexander G. Gavriliuk Role: Ivan A. Trojan Role: Dymitro A. Dzivenko Role: Reinhard Boehler Role: The team experimentally demonstrated single bonded cubic gauche Nitrogen. ([NOAA][3]) The legacy ozone geometry also checks out: NIST’s CCCBDB experimental geometry gives 1.278 Å O–O distance and 116.8° O–O–O angle, and NIST’s WebBook lists the three principal ozone fundamentals at about 1103, 701 and 1042 cm⁻¹ . ([CCCBDB][4]) Evaluated nuclear data and review The NUBASE2020 nuclear state catalogue provides 24 evaluated states with uncertainties, qualifiers and source line provenance. This dated evaluation does not make the whole material record complete.

docs.text: Oxygen — People and Intellectual Lineage Carl Wilhelm Scheele Role: Scheele produced Oxygen before Priestley's published report, probably by 1771. His account appeared later. MAT edge: Joseph Priestley Role: Priestley prepared the gas in 1774 and published his observations. He interpreted it within phlogiston theory as: MAT therefore separates: from: Antoine Lavoisier Role: Lavoisier incorporated Oxygen into a new account of combustion and oxidation and introduced the name: The historical belief that Oxygen was universally the acid forming principle was later shown to be incorrect. MAT lineage: Source: Friedrich Hund Role: Hund's quantum mechanical work forms part of the intellectual lineage of molecular electronic state descriptions. Robert S. Mulliken Role: Mulliken received the 1966 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for work on chemical bonds and molecular electronic structure by the molecular orbital method. Source: Respiration Otto Heinrich Warburg Role: Warburg received the 1931 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for work on the nature and mode of action of the respiratory enzyme. MAT relationship: Source: Photosynthetic Oxygen Evolution Robert Hill Role: Hill showed that isolated chloroplasts can evolve Oxygen during the light reactions in the presence of suitable electron acceptors without simultaneous CO2 fixation. CALC-001 — Fluorine-18 Decay Energetics
docs.text: CALC 001 — Fluorine 18 Decay Energetics Parent: {}^{18}F Daughter: {}^{18}O Neutral atomic masses: M({}^{18}F)=18.00093733\ u M({}^{18}O)=17.99915961286\ u Atomic mass difference: Q {\rm EC} = [M({}^{18}F) M({}^{18}O)]c^2 \boxed{ Q {\rm EC} \approx1.65593\ {\rm MeV} } For positron emission: Q {\beta^+} = [M({}^{18}F) M({}^{18}O) 2m e]c^2 giving: \boxed{ Q {\beta^+} \approx0.63394\ {\rm MeV} } This corresponds to the approximate positron endpoint before nuclear recoil corrections. Decay branches: Important distinction: The positron subsequently annihilates with an electron, typically producing two approximately: 511\ {\rm keV} photons. The ¹⁸F decay branch used above is supported by radionuclide standardization work: roughly 96.86% β⁺ and 3.14% electron capture ; TUNL’s dedicated half life evaluation recommends 109.732 ± 0.011 min . ([ScienceDirect][2]) The F₂ counterexample also becomes stronger numerically: modern work gives \(D 0(F 2)\) around 154.92 ± 0.10 kJ/mol , reinforcing the original conclusion that Fluorine's extraordinary chemical reactivity does not originate from an exceptionally strong F–F bond. ([ACS Publications][3]) HF, by comparison, has \(r e=0.916808\) Å, \(\omega e=4138.32\ {\rm cm^{ 1}}\), and \(B e=20.9557\ {\rm cm^{ 1}}\) in the NIST diatomic compilation. ([NIST WebBook][4])

docs.title: Sodium — Additional Research Notes
docs.text: Sodium — Additional Research Notes Imported research; scientific review pending. These cross domain notes were supplied after the Sodium 24 calculation in 42.txt. They retain conversation provenance, not independent validation. For ²³Na itself, the nuclear spin is \(I=3/2\), so it is both NMR active and quadrupolar; its Larmor frequency scales with magnetic field rather than being a fixed “Sodium frequency.” The ground state atomic hyperfine constant is about 885.813 MHz , while the D line excited states introduce additional magnetic dipole and electric quadrupole structure. That makes Sodium a particularly useful bridge between atomic spectroscopy and condensed/biological NMR. Liquid Sodium is similarly state specific. Argonne's current Cardinal implementation derives density, enthalpy, heat capacity and thermal conductivity from the Fink–Leibowitz Sodium correlations rather than treating these as fixed constants. The NaK implementation likewise treats eutectic NaK with a potassium mass fraction of 0.778 , reinforcing the legacy point that alloying can dramatically alter the accessible liquid range.

Electron count is calculated as Z−q. This is not a bulk work function or electrochemical potential. Square brackets retain semiempirical estimates; parentheses retain theoretical values. Unbracketed values retain their evaluated status. Ground configurations describe dominant calculated components and may have uncertain assignments. NIST notation is preserved. Numeric uncertainty is transcribed in eV; unavailable uncertainty remains UNKNOWN. No confidence level, isotope assignment or extra precision is inferred. Retrieved 2026 09 08. Every structured entry preserves the original line and its line number. The parser is checked against the source's published column specification and representative ground states, isomers, estimates and stable states. Post 2020 findings and supplied research batches retain separate provenance and review status. Derived decay metrics The structured evaluation now includes a decay constant and mean lifetime for each positive numeric half life. These use the single exponential model, \(\lambda=\ln(2)/T {1/2}\) and \(\tau=T {1/2}/\ln(2)\). Values retain the original time unit: a half life in years produces a rate per source year, without silently assuming a calendar conversion. Inequalities reverse for the reciprocal decay constant. Estimates remain estimates. Stable or unavailable half lives have no numeric result. Symmetric uncertainty is propagated to first order; asymmetric source uncertainties remain unpropagated and visible. These calculations add no new experimental evidence or significant figures. Atomic masses, Q values and separation energies are available in the separate AME2020 companion, with ground state, estimate and uncertainty semantics.

Derived decay metrics The structured evaluation now includes a decay constant and mean lifetime for each positive numeric half life. These use the single exponential model, \(\lambda=\ln(2)/T {1/2}\) and \(\tau=T {1/2}/\ln(2)\). Values retain the original time unit: a half life in years produces a rate per source year, without silently assuming a calendar conversion. Inequalities reverse for the reciprocal decay constant. Retrieved 2026 09 08. Every structured entry preserves the original line and its line number. The parser is checked against the source's published column specification and representative ground states, isomers, estimates and stable states. Post 2020 findings and supplied research batches retain separate provenance and review status. Derived decay metrics The structured evaluation now includes a decay constant and mean lifetime for each positive numeric half life. These use the single exponential model, \(\lambda=\ln(2)/T {1/2}\) and \(\tau=T {1/2}/\ln(2)\). Values retain the original time unit: a half life in years produces a rate per source year, without silently assuming a calendar conversion. Inequalities reverse for the reciprocal decay constant. Estimates remain estimates. Stable or unavailable half lives have no numeric result. Symmetric uncertainty is propagated to first order; asymmetric source uncertainties remain unpropagated and visible. These calculations add no new experimental evidence or significant figures. Atomic masses, Q values and separation energies are available in the separate AME2020 companion, with ground state, estimate and uncertainty semantics.

Derived decay metrics The structured evaluation now includes a decay constant and mean lifetime for each positive numeric half life. Values retain the original time unit: a half life in years produces a rate per source year, without silently assuming a calendar conversion. Inequalities reverse for the reciprocal decay constant.
